cards.text: Welcome to Mags' station, friend, where the words ring out LOUD. Jesus is traveling through the towns and villages, teaching as He makes His way toward Jerusalem. Then someone asks Him, "Lord, will only a few people be saved?"

cards.question: Jesus doesn't give that person a head count. Instead He tells them to make every effort to enter through what?
Jesus says many will try to enter through that narrow door and will not be able.

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a picture. The master of the house gets up and shuts the door, and people stand outside knocking and saying, "Lord, open the door for us."

cards.question: The door is shut and the people outside are knocking. What does the master of the house tell them?

answers.text: I do not know where you are from
Come back again in the morning
Wait there until I call for you

cards.text: So the folks outside pull out their résumé: we ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets. Friend, that's like asking for the corner office because you once waved at the boss in the parking lot.

cards.question: Once the people outside remind the master that they ate and drank with him, he opens the door and lets them in.

cards.text: The master doesn't budge: "I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers." And Jesus says there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

cards.question: Jesus says the ones thrown out will see some familiar faces inside the kingdom of God. Who will they see?

answers.text: Israel's forefathers and all the prophets
The Pharisees and all the scribes
The kings of Israel and all the priests

cards.text: That's Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Israel's forefathers, along with all the prophets. Then Jesus mentions a table in the kingdom of God, and friend, you KNOW this old stamper just leaned all the way in.

cards.question: Jesus says people will come and recline at the table in the kingdom of God. Where will they come from?

answers.text: East and west and north and south

cards.question: Then Jesus sums it up: "And indeed, some who are ___ will be ___, and some who are first will be last."

cards.text: At that very hour, some Pharisees show up. They're a group of religious leaders, and they've got a warning for Jesus about Herod, the ruler of Galilee (Luke 3:1).

cards.question: The Pharisees tell Jesus to leave and get away because Herod wants to kill Him.

cards.text: Friend, I jump when my oven timer DINGS. Jesus hears that Herod wants Him dead, and He just says, "Go tell that fox."

cards.question: Jesus sends a message to Herod. What does He say He'll keep doing today and tomorrow?

answers.text: Driving out demons and healing people
Staying out of sight in the villages

cards.question: Jesus says He must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, "for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of ___."

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks to the city itself: "O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her..." I don't know about you, friend, but I hear heartbreak in that.

cards.question: Jesus says He has often longed to gather Jerusalem's children together. What does He compare it to?

answers.text: A hen gathering her chicks under her wings
A shepherd gathering his sheep into the fold
A fisherman gathering his nets into the boat

cards.question: Jesus says Jerusalem was willing to be gathered together.

cards.text: Nope. In Jesus' words, "you were unwilling!" Then He says, "Look, your house is left to you desolate."

cards.question: Jesus tells Jerusalem they won't see Him again until they say something. What will they say?

answers.text: Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord
Truly this was the Son of God
We have no king but Caesar

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The fill in the blank quotes Jesus' line from 13:30, which the baker hasn't seen, and asks for its exact words. The second half of the same line, 'some who are first will be last,' is printed in the question. It mirrors the blanks, so the answer is handed over by wording rather than reasoned from meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The right answer calls Abraham, Isaac and Jacob 'Israel's forefathers,' and card 10 repeats it. That fact comes from outside the passage and has no reference. It also isn't what the text calls them, since 13:28 names them.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This card introduces Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as 'Israel's forefathers.' That is a fact from outside the passage, and it has no reference.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'East and west and north and south,' has a sweeping four-direction rhythm that sounds like the Bible. The two wrong answers are short and plain and sound like each other. The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card describes the Pharisees as 'a group of religious leaders.' That fact comes from outside the passage, and it has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The setup says the Pharisees have 'a warning for Jesus about Herod.' That all but gives away the true or false on card 2, which asks whether they tell Him to leave because Herod wants to kill Him.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Jesus says in 13:32 that 'on the third day I will reach My goal,' but no card ever tells this. Card 4 asks only about 'today and tomorrow,' so the baker misses an important detail of Jesus' reply to Herod.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
